description: Gmail connection is started, confirmed and disconnected by the business owner only, and a Gmail OAuth callback links nothing until the user who started it confirms it (COST-LEDGER-001 section 7 items 4 and 5; R0-07 review ST-2 and ST-3). GET /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail/auth-url, the new POST /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail/confirm and DELETE /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail carry AuthGuard + BusinessGuard and GmailService.assertConnectAuthority: the OWNER membership or Business.ownerId (the rule IdentityService.assertBusinessOwner applies) and SUPER_ADMIN (the BusinessGuard platform bypass); every other member gets 403 {code:'GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY'}. The signed OAuth state (HMAC-SHA256 with GOOGLE_STATE_SECRET, single use per process as R0-07 made it) now carries the initiating user id, the business id, a nonce and a 10-minute expiry. GET /commerce/gmail/callback stays public (Google redirects the browser; the web proxy forwards no session) and links nothing: a verified state that names a user has its code exchanged and the tokens stored as a PENDING connector_accounts row (provider GOOGLE, service GMAIL, tokens encrypted with encryptToken, settings {purpose, userId, nonce, pendingExpiresAt} with a 15-minute window; existing table, no schema change), then redirects gmail=pending&pending=<id>. Only that user, still the owner (or SUPER_ADMIN), confirming that id on that business within the window, once, activates it (Business.gmail*); anything else answers 404 {code:'GMAIL_PENDING_NOT_FOUND'} and links nothing. An expired, replayed, forged or user-less state redirects gmail=error&reason=invalid_state with no token exchange. Google's token exchange and userinfo are stubbed in process (no network). Run from apps/server against this packet's isolated, migrated database: npx vitest run test/gmail-connect-binding.integration.test.ts src/modules/commerce/gmail.service.spec.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-cmf5-vitest.json, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/gmail-connect-binding.json --report .proof/r0-cmf5-vitest.json. Every case of the two files is required and no other case is admitted (allowAdditionalCases false: the two it.todo follow-ups are now real cases, D-I and the web suite); requireReportSuccess keeps every reported case binding. RED-BEFORE on pkt/R0-CMF4-SEND-EMAIL-ORDER-repair (acfda3e6; tests-first commit c788e635): the integration suite failed 19 of 25 (STAFF auth-url 200 with a Google URL; ADMIN and STAFF revenue:admin 200; the state named no user; the distinguished owner 403 from ModuleScopeGuard; the owner's state completed in a stranger's request redirected gmail=success and linked the stranger's mailbox; a signed user-less state linked; no confirm route; STAFF revenue:write DELETE gmail 200 and cleared the mailbox; B05 and B12 failed there only because their first step expects gmail=pending) and the spec failed 9 of 9. Passing on the base (negative controls): X01, A06 (non-member 403, anonymous 401), B06 (expired state), B07 (forged or edited state), C02 (owner disconnect), X02 (no outbound beyond the Google stub). REVIEW REPAIRS (pkt/R0-CMF5-GMAIL-CONNECT-BINDING-repair; R0-CMF5 review ST-CMF5-1..5, CR-CMF5-1..5): GET /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail/pending/:id (OWNER only, bound to the user the state names, returns the staged mailbox and no token) and POST .../gmail/confirm now requires {pendingId, email}, email equal (case-insensitively) to the staged mailbox, else 409 GMAIL_PENDING_EMAIL_MISMATCH and the row stays (D01-D03, U11); both callbacks refuse a request whose ambient tenant (TenantInterceptor) is not the state's business, before any token exchange, proved with TenantInterceptor as APP_INTERCEPTOR and the Prisma tenant context provider installed for the whole suite (E01-E02, H03, U10); confirm (connect/replace) and every disconnect write one team_activity_logs row naming the actor in the change's transaction (F01, I02, U12); PENDING rows past their window are swept on stage, preview, confirm and status, and a disconnect removes every PENDING Gmail row of the business (G01-G03, U13-U14); POST /connect/google-suite/businesses/:b/auth-url applies the Gmail owner rule whenever gmail is requested (the default set includes it), its state names the caller, and its callback stages a Gmail grant as the same PENDING connection (redirect /app/commerce?gmail=pending) instead of writing Business.gmail*; POST /connectors/businesses/:b/disconnect|reconnect/gmail go through GmailService.disconnectGmail (owner rule, pending removal, audit) before the registry (H01-H04, I01-I02). RED-BEFORE on pkt/R0-CMF5-GMAIL-CONNECT-BINDING (929fd95d) with the repaired tests: 20 of 54 failed (D01-D03, E01, F01, G01, G03, H01-H04, I01-I02, X02 and U10-U14; E02 failed there only through E01's residue and is now independent); G02 passed on the base (the base already removed rows older than the window on a new stage). REVIEW 2 REPAIRS (pkt/R0-CMF5-GMAIL-CONNECT-BINDING-repair2; SEC-CMF5-R1..R4, CMF5R-1..3): a Google Suite state is single use per process and carries purpose google-suite; the suite callback accepts only that purpose with a valid service list and the commerce callback only purpose gmail, so a member's calendar-only suite state no longer stages a Gmail connection and a commerce state no longer has its code exchanged at the suite callback (H05-H06, U15); confirm and disconnect lock the business row first (SELECT ... FOR NO KEY UPDATE) so they no longer deadlock (J02, U17); a consent with no refresh token is linked only as a re-consent of the stored mailbox, else 409 GMAIL_PENDING_NO_REFRESH_TOKEN and the stored mailbox stays whole (J01, U16); a Google Suite Gmail grant keeps the live Gmail check the callback made and, on the owner's confirmation, writes the gmail connector_statuses row (connected with intake on, or error) and a connector activity row as the sign-in did before (H07, U18). RED-BEFORE on 97669ec8 (tests-first commit 3d718f40): 9 of 63 failed (H05-H07, J01, J02 with 8 of 16 trials deadlocked, 7 of them disconnect 500 with the mailbox left linked, U15-U18); every earlier case passed there. R0-CMF6-GMAIL-CONNECTOR-ROUTES (cases K01-K05, L01-L02; RED-BEFORE found by the CMF5 verification, wf_84ed7b52-835): on the generic connector surface, POST /connectors/businesses/:b/smoke/gmail (the GmailConnector smoke test sends a marked self-test email from the business mailbox) and .../sync/gmail (reads the business inbox into Key Inbox) had only AuthGuard + BusinessGuard, so any member could send from and read the mailbox; they now follow the Gmail owner rule (GmailService.assertConnectAuthority via resolveGmailService, 403 GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY before the registry is reached). test/gmail (the Gmail profile check: it sends nothing and reads no message, the same check health-check/run and the health monitor make), health/gmail, statuses, dashboard and authenticate/gmail (status reads) are unchanged, as is every other connector (google_calendar control). DELETE /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail (GmailService.disconnectGmail, also behind the connector disconnect/reconnect routes) now marks the gmail connector_statuses row disconnected in the disconnect's own transaction (proved by one xmin on the business row, the connector row and the audit row) and writes no row when there is none, so a mailbox connected through the Google Suite sign-in and disconnected there is no longer selected by the nightly sync. For these cases the connector routes that act on a connector reach a real ConnectorRegistryService holding the real GmailConnector (its smoke test sends through the stubbed Gmail API, which records every message) and a google_calendar control connector; the GmailConnector's inbox ingestion is a stand-in recording each read. RED-BEFORE on claude/elegant-curie-7azpsb (61baa48d; tests-first commit a935d881): 3 of 52 integration cases failed (K01, K02, L01); K03-K05, L02 and every R0-CMF5 case passed. R0-CMF6 review repairs (cases L03, M01, M02; RED-BEFORE on the packet head d557acf0: L03 and M01 failed, M02 and every other case passed, L04 todo): DELETE /connectors/businesses/:b/credentials/gmail (it marks the gmail connector row disconnected and clears its account) follows the Gmail owner rule, 403 GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY before anything is written (SEC-CMF6-1; the owner and a SUPER_ADMIN keep the route; other connectors are not gated); PATCH .../inbox-config/gmail stays open to members (M02 control: it writes the Key Inbox processing settings only, never the row's status, account or connection time); a commerce confirmation updates an existing gmail connector row to the confirmed mailbox (connected, the address, a fresh connection time, no error, intake kept) in its own transaction and writes none when there is none, so a mailbox disconnected and connected again through the commerce flow is selected by the nightly sync again (CR-CMF6-1).
notes: Owner ruling D-11 (2026-10-31): business configuration is OWNER only. The mailbox invoices, reminders, receipts and quotes are sent from (GmailService.sendEmail) is business configuration, so connecting, replacing and disconnecting it follows D-11, as R0-08c did for plan changes. The rule is restated in GmailService.assertConnectAuthority (CommerceModule does not import IdentityModule), with the same two owner arms and the SUPER_ADMIN bypass. ModuleScopeGuard was removed from auth-url and DELETE gmail: a revenue scope admits no one the owner rule refuses, and ModuleScopeGuard refused a distinguished owner with no membership row. GET .../gmail/status and the inbox and send routes keep their revenue scopes.

PENDING storage: connector_accounts (ConnectorAccount) is an existing tenant-scoped table with no other reader or writer in apps/server; its token columns are ciphertext by contract (token-encryption-coverage HANDLED_ELSEWHERE), so the pending tokens go through core/crypto/token-crypto encryptToken and are decrypted only at confirmation, when they move to the Business.gmail* columns the Prisma token-encryption extension encrypts. Every call names businessId. A newer consent by the same user replaces that user's unconfirmed pending row, and pending rows of the business past the window are removed when a new one is staged. The pending id is gmc_ plus 24 random bytes (base64url) and reaches only the browser that completed consent.

The callback cannot be bound to a session on this base: the API authenticates by Bearer token only and the web proxy (apps/web/src/app/api/commerce/gmail/callback/route.ts) fetches the API server-to-server with no session, so binding is by the state's userId plus the authenticated confirmation. A foreign user's confirmation is refused at confirm time (403 GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY for a non-owner, 404 GMAIL_PENDING_NOT_FOUND for an owner or SUPER_ADMIN who is not the user the state names); the callback itself redirects gmail=error for expired, replayed, forged and user-less states.

Review repairs extended the write set (recorded as a deviation): core/connectors/google-suite.controller.ts, core/connectors/google-suite.service.ts and core/connectors/connector.controller.ts (ST-CMF5-1), and apps/web/src/app/app/commerce/hooks/use-commerce-integrations.ts, apps/web/src/app/app/marketing/hooks/use-marketing.ts, apps/web/src/app/app/commerce/page.tsx with apps/web/src/app/app/commerce/__tests__/gmail-connect-confirm.test.tsx (CR-CMF5-1, CR-CMF5-2: the owner's confirm step reads gmail=pending&pending=<id>, previews, asks 'Connect <email>?' and POSTs {pendingId, email}; GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY refusals are shown, never reported as success). ConnectorModule (core, global) does not import CommerceModule, so the connector routes resolve GmailService from the application container (ModuleRef, strict false) and fail closed with 503 when it is absent.

Review 2 (repair2): SEC-CMF5-R3 needed a product call. The safer behaviour is kept: a consent that returned no refresh token is linked only as a re-consent of the mailbox already stored (it keeps that mailbox's refresh token, as before R0-CMF5); for another mailbox, or with none stored, the confirmation is refused (409 GMAIL_PENDING_NO_REFRESH_TOKEN) and nothing changes, because such a mailbox could never send once its access token expired. CMF5R-1: only a Google Suite staging (origin google-suite on the PENDING row, with the live check's result and no token) writes the gmail connector rows on confirmation; the commerce Gmail flow still writes none, as on the base. CMF5R-2 and CMF5R-3 are web-only (core-channels-section.tsx retries a GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY refusal of the default sign-in with every service but gmail; the commerce confirm is sent once per pending id and ConfirmDialog gained a busy prop that disables its confirm button); their cases are apps/web/src/app/app/key-connect/__tests__/core-channels-google-sign-in.test.tsx (W09-W11) and W08 in the commerce web suite, outside this manifest's two files.

R0-CMF6: the server's refusal of the default Google Suite service set for non-owners (the web retries without gmail) is unchanged, as the packet requires. Not changed and left for a product call: PATCH /connectors/businesses/:b/inbox-config/gmail (any member toggles whether the mailbox's items are processed by Key Inbox; a config write that neither sends nor reads) and POST .../authenticate/gmail emitting connector.connected (a 'connect' activity row with no actor) when a mailbox is stored. disconnectGmail marks the row with one raw UPDATE inside its transaction (as lockBusinessRow is raw) rather than connectorStatus.updateMany, because gmail.service.spec.ts's recording transaction (outside this packet's write set) has no connectorStatus.updateMany; the row's other columns (connected_account, intake_enabled) are left as GmailConnector.disconnect leaves them.

R0-CMF6 review: SEC-CMF6-2 (a gmail sync or smoke test already running when the owner disconnects writes the row connected again) was not fixed in R0-CMF6 (outside its write set) and was tracked as the it.todo [R0-CMF6-L04]; R0-CMF6b fixes it (see the R0-CMF6b note), L04 is a required case and allowAdditionalCases is false again. The CR-CMF6-1 update is one raw UPDATE inside the confirmation's transaction (as markGmailConnectorDisconnected), so U18's commerce branch still sees no connectorStatus upsert and no activity row: the commerce confirmation creates no row, as on the base.

R0-CMF6b-GMAIL-SYNC-RACE (review SEC-CMF6-2): GmailIngestionService.syncInbox (its final connected or error write) and ConnectorRegistryService.smokeTestConnector (its success write, for gmail) wrote the gmail connector row unconditionally once they finished, so a run that started before the owner disconnected the mailbox wrote the row connected again after the disconnect had marked it disconnected (or created one when there was none) and the nightly sync selected a mailbox that was gone. That write is now made in one short transaction that first takes the business row lock GmailService.disconnectGmail takes (SELECT ... FOR NO KEY UPDATE, as lockBusinessRow) and writes only while the business still has its mailbox (businesses.gmail_access_token set, what GmailConnector.isConnected reads): a disconnect that committed first is seen and nothing is written; one that starts later waits and marks the row disconnected after it. A sync whose write was skipped reports success false ('Gmail was disconnected while this sync ran'); a smoke test reports what its connector did (the self-test was sent) and only its status write is skipped. Other connector types keep the unconditional smoke write. Cases L04 (sync race), L05 (smoke race), L06 (no row; a sync failing after the disconnect) and L07 (control: with the mailbox linked the writes are made as before); the sync reaches the REAL GmailIngestionService through the owner's POST .../sync/gmail, with the stubbed Gmail profile and inbox list (held open by the case). No schema change.

R0-CMF6b review repairs (SEC-CMF6b-1..3, CR-CMF6b-1; cases L08-L10). The linked-mailbox check of the guarded final writes (GmailIngestionService.writeStatusWhileMailboxLinked, ConnectorRegistryService.writeWhileGmailMailboxLinked) read gmail_access_token, the one mailbox column a token refresh writes back (GoogleTokenHelper.getValidAccessToken, an unlocked business.update), so a sync whose refresh was in flight over the disconnect marked the row connected again (L08); it now reads gmail_refresh_token and gmail_email (as GmailService.getGmailStatus does), which a refresh never writes. A sync or smoke test binds the mailbox it acts on (gmail_email while a refresh token is stored) before it reads a token, and its write is made only while lower(gmail_email) is still that mailbox, so a run over a disconnect and a new connection no longer writes the old address and history cursor onto the new mailbox's row (L09). A sync re-checks that binding after its token read and before every message read and every filing, and stops (no cursor stored, success false, the disconnected message) once the mailbox is gone, so it no longer reads or files messages after the owner disconnects (L10). An access token such a refresh leaves on a cleared mailbox (no refresh token, no address) is cleared under the same lock, so GmailConnector.healthCheck (which reads gmail_access_token) does not report the disconnected mailbox as connected. A sync of a business with no linked mailbox at its start fails with 'Gmail not connected' (the message GoogleTokenHelper gave) and writes no error row. Residuals outside the write set: GoogleTokenHelper and GmailService.getValidAccessToken still write a refreshed access token back unconditionally (only a sync clears what it finds); GmailConnector.smokeTest, testConnection and isConnected still read gmail_access_token; collectInboxInputs (GmailConnector.syncToIngestion, which has no caller) is unchanged; a message whose filing check passed just before a disconnect committed can still be filed (the Key Inbox write is not under the business row lock).

R0-CMF6c-GMAIL-TOKEN-REFRESH-CAS (the R0-CMF6b residual; cases N01-N04, the it.todo N05). GmailService.getValidAccessToken read the stored refresh token, awaited Google's refresh_token grant, then wrote the new access token and expiry back with an unconditional business.update({where:{id}}), so a disconnect committed during the refresh round trip was overwritten (the disconnected business held a live access token again and the request read the mailbox with it, N01) and a disconnect plus a connection of another mailbox got the old mailbox's token written over the new one's (the send went out with the old mailbox's token under the new address, N02). The write is now a compare-and-set: in one short transaction that first takes the business row lock disconnectGmail and confirmPendingConnection take (lockBusinessRow, SELECT ... FOR NO KEY UPDATE), the row is re-read through the Prisma token-encryption extension and written (business.update, so the extension encrypts the token) only while gmail_refresh_token (decrypted) and gmail_email are still the ones the refresh used. The predicate is the stored refresh token plus the address, not the address alone, so a re-consent of the same mailbox (a new refresh token) also wins over an older refresh (N04). It is not a SQL equality on the column: the tokens are AES-GCM ciphertext with a random IV (a where-equality on the plaintext never matches) and updateMany bypasses the encryption extension (it would store the token in plaintext). A lost race writes nothing and re-reads once: no mailbox answers 503 provider_not_configured 'Gmail not connected' (N01); another connection's still-valid token is used (N02, N04); a second lost race also answers 'Gmail not connected'. N03 is the control (no change in flight: written back encrypted as before, reused until it expires). Census of the other writers of gmail_access_token: confirmPendingConnection and disconnectGmail (the connection changes themselves, under the same lock); GmailConnector.disconnect (writes null only, a disconnect: a refresh in flight over it now loses, the refresh token it clears is part of the predicate); GmailIngestionService.writeStatusWhileMailboxLinked (writes null only, under the lock, only on a row with no refresh token and no address); GoogleSuiteService.handleCallback (never writes Business.gmail*: a Gmail grant is staged through GmailService.stagePendingTokens); GoogleTokenHelper.getValidAccessToken (gmail fields, used by GmailIngestionService.syncInbox and collectInboxInputs) is NOT safe and is outside this write set: its refresh write-back is still unconditional, so a sync's refresh over a disconnect plus a new connection writes the old mailbox's token onto the new row; tracked as the it.todo [R0-CMF6c-N05], not a required case, and allowAdditionalCases is true for that one it.todo only (the R0-CMF6 L04 precedent); the follow-up that fixes it turns N05 into a required case and sets allowAdditionalCases back to false. RED-BEFORE on claude/elegant-curie-7azpsb (d78f591a) with the tests-first commit: N01, N02 and N04 failed, N03 passed. No schema change.
